disposition_reason: Table 1 prints overall mean, range and origin-group means for trace elements including lead, arsenic, cadmium and mercury in 21 retail dried black soldier fly larvae products.

study.design: retail survey of dried black soldier fly larvae products sold for backyard poultry, US, 2023-2024
study.origin: as labeled: China (13), North America (4), unidentified (5)
study.market: US retail stores and online establishments
study.method: Commercial accredited lab; As, Cd, Pb, Hg by AOAC 2011.19, 993.14 and 2015.01 (ICP-MS); other elements by modified AOAC 984.27/985.01
study.lod_text: heavy metals LOD 2.5-10 ppb (per AOAC methods)
study.qa: blinded subsamples sent to ISO-accredited contract laboratory; no recoveries reported

controls.control: Country of origin of dried black soldier fly larvae
controls.comparator: North American-origin products (n=4) vs Chinese-origin products (n=13)
controls.outcome: Pb 31.0 vs 784 ppb (about 25x; p=0.266); As 62.0 vs 511 ppb (about 8x; p=0.195); Cd 196 vs 260 ppb (p=0.576); text says the differences were not statistically significant because of high variation among Chinese-origin products

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Authors' proposed maximum levels for dried black soldier fly larvae (not regulatory)
regulatory_or_exposure.value: Pb 1000 ppb, As 1000 ppb, Cd 200 ppb, Hg 50 ppb

unresolved: Group counts printed as 13 + 4 + 5 = 22 but the text says 21 samples; overall n recorded as 21.
The abstract calls the lead and arsenic differences statistically different, but Table 1 prints p = 0.266 (Pb) and 0.195 (As) and the discussion says there was no statistical difference.
Products are animal feed (poultry supplements), not human food; recorded under their printed label as a proxy for edible insects.
Values for the five unidentified-origin products are not printed separately.
